hero.headline: Martin County deputies capture Palm City hit-and-run suspect after hours-long swamp search
hero.teaser: Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies captured a hit-and-run suspect Wednesday evening after searching for more than two hours through miles of swamp along the Martin County-St.
hero.body:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies captured a hit-and-run suspect Wednesday evening after searching for more than two hours through miles of swamp along the Martin County-St. Lucie County line. The suspect fled a hit-and-run incident in the area of Southwest Rivers End Way in Palm City and was last seen running westbound into the Windstone Community.

 The sheriff's office announced just before 6:15 p.m. Wednesday that the suspect was in law enforcement custody. The sheriff's office confirmed the suspect's identity as 39-year-old Likenson Daceus of Fort Pierce. Deputies described him as a Black man wearing a black shirt with blue writing on the back and black pants.

 Multiple K-9 units were deployed in the search along with air support to establish a large perimeter. The Martin County Sheriff's Office received assistance from its aviation, drone, and K-9 units, the Port St. Lucie Police Department and Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission officers.

 The sheriff's office said the manhunt lasted more than two hours through the large swamp area spanning the county line. Deputies used multiple tracking methods to locate Daceus in the difficult terrain before taking him into custody Wednesday evening.

cards.headline: New Florida emergency chief inherits 41-day overdue accounting for disaster fund
cards.teaser: Florida's new emergency management director Jared Perdue took control of an agency that failed to deliver a required financial report on the state's Emergency Preparedness and Resp
cards.body:
Florida's new emergency management director Jared Perdue took control of an agency that failed to deliver a required financial report on the state's Emergency Preparedness and Response Fund, now 41 days past its legal deadline. A dozen Democratic lawmakers wrote to Perdue on Aug. 25 saying the Florida Division of Emergency Management never provided the quarterly accounting mandated under SB 7040, which required the first report by July 15. The report must detail the fund's projected year-end balance, cash-flow statements, federal reimbursements, an itemized list of purchased assets and unpaid invoices.

 The fund has faced mounting scrutiny after more than $4.7 billion flowed through it since 2022, prompting lawmakers to debate tighter controls. Lawmakers say approximately $566 million was spent on immigration enforcement during the last fiscal year. An earlier FDEM annual report showed more than $573 million in immigration-related spending since 2023, including detention facilities, aircraft, vehicles and deployments of Florida personnel to Texas. FDEM told lawmakers it transmitted information on July 28, but the legislators said the materials consisted of five spreadsheets cataloging disaster spending and did not include the inventory, assets and pending invoices required under the new law.

 Perdue, the longtime Florida Department of Transportation secretary, assumed the emergency management role after Kevin Guthrie resigned during hurricane season to join Lt. Gov. Jay Collins' unsuccessful campaign for governor.

 At his first press conference in the new role, Perdue promised both agencies would keep moving. Gov. Ron DeSantis said Wednesday that more than $100 million in federal immigration enforcement reimbursements has been repaid and that the overdue report is moving through the administration. DeSantis argued that Florida's multibillion-dollar reserves mean the state is not facing an immediate cash crunch.

 The lawmakers' letter asks Perdue to provide the complete report by the end of August, explain the delay, account for outstanding contractor obligations and reconcile federal reimbursements that have been requested, approved, received, denied or remain pending. Rep. Anna Eskamani, D-Orlando, who organized the letter, said lawmakers remain hopeful Perdue will comply but indicated they are considering legal action.

 Florida has sought federal money to cover much of the immigration enforcement cost. Previous court filings raised questions about whether the state would receive the full $608 million reimbursement it expected and whether federal money could cover construction expenses.

cards.headline: Gov. DeSantis orders Florida flags to half-staff following Dolly Parton's death
cards.teaser: Gov. Ron DeSantis on Tuesday ordered flags across Florida lowered to half-staff following the death of country music icon Dolly Parton.
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis on Tuesday ordered flags across the state to be lowered to half-staff following the death of country music icon Dolly Parton. The governor's office said the order follows a directive from the president and applies to U.S. and Florida flags at all state and local government buildings, installations and grounds. The flags will remain at half-staff until sunset Sept. 1.

 Parton died peacefully Tuesday in Nashville at age 80, according to her publicist. The Tennessee native became one of the most recognizable figures in country music during a career that spanned decades. She wrote hundreds of songs, including Jolene, Coat of Many Colors and I Will Always Love You, while also building a career in film, business and philanthropy. Parton was also known for founding the Imagination Library, which provides free books to children, and for opening Dollywood in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee.

cards.headline: All 36 Border Collies from Palm City case surrendered to Humane Society, adoptions begin Sept. 1
cards.teaser: All 36 Border Collies removed from a Southwest Alligator Street home in Palm City earlier this month have been legally surrendered, clearing the way for adoptions beginning Sept. 1.
cards.body:
All 36 Border Collies removed from a Southwest Alligator Street home in Palm City on Aug. 10 have been legally surrendered to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast. Investigators found the dogs living without air conditioning and surrounded by feces, urine-soaked materials and debris. Many arrived at the shelter dirty, severely matted and covered in dried waste.

Shelter staff have removed the dogs' matted fur and cleaned away layers of dried feces as the animals recover. The dogs have received several baths, vaccinations and veterinary care. Some have been treated for skin infections, body sores, eye infections and intestinal parasites. Two of the Border Collies are still struggling, are very withdrawn and don't make eye contact, while others are perking up and appear to be friendly.

Adoption applications for the Border Collies will be available beginning Sept. 1 through the Humane Society's website and Facebook page. Adoption fees will be $140 for adult Border Collies and $175 for puppies. Paige ODonnell, 62, was arrested in the case and faces 72 charges including 36 third-degree felony counts of animal cruelty. Her bond was set at $270,000.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man charged with manslaughter after BB gun shooting
cards.teaser: A 36-year-old Fort Pierce man faces manslaughter charges after police say he fatally shot a 34-year-old man with a BB gun Saturday near an elementary school.
cards.body:
Jabari Cowart has been charged with manslaughter after Fort Pierce police say he fatally shot a 34-year-old man with a BB gun on Saturday in the 2900 block of Avenue G. Police said a group of men in their 30s had been shooting a BB gun at trees when Cowart asked to use the weapon and later pointed it at one of the men before pulling the trigger. The victim fell to the ground and officers were called to the scene.

Ken Noble, marketing manager at The Tactical Store in Fort Pierce, said BB guns can be extremely dangerous. Noble explained that BB guns can cause serious injury or death because they fire metal projectiles at high speed. He said anything moving fast enough can penetrate skin and hit vital spots.

Cowart is being held at the St. Lucie County jail. Noble advised that people should not point any weapon at anyone and should follow safety procedures when handling firearms, including BB guns.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man charged with manslaughter after BB gun shooting
hero.teaser: A 36-year-old Fort Pierce man faces manslaughter charges after police say he fatally shot a 34-year-old man with a BB gun Saturday near an elementary school.
hero.body:
Jabari Cowart has been charged with manslaughter after Fort Pierce police say he fatally shot a 34-year-old man with a BB gun on Saturday in the 2900 block of Avenue G. Police said a group of men in their 30s had been shooting a BB gun at trees when Cowart asked to use the weapon and later pointed it at one of the men before pulling the trigger. The victim fell to the ground and officers were called to the scene.

Ken Noble, marketing manager at The Tactical Store in Fort Pierce, said BB guns can be extremely dangerous. Noble explained that BB guns can cause serious injury or death because they fire metal projectiles at high speed. He said anything moving fast enough can penetrate skin and hit vital spots.

Cowart is being held at the St. Lucie County jail. Noble advised that people should not point any weapon at anyone and should follow safety procedures when handling firearms, including BB guns.
